actions.body: Research into the foundations of artificial moral agency clarifies that ethical failures are often governance failures rooted in human design choices. By situating artificial agents within a historical context of delegated authority, we find that accountability arrangements—not machine malice—are the primary locus of risk. Furthermore, interpreting AI outputs through a pragmatic semiotic lens reveals that epistemic processes like evaluation and justification remain fundamentally human-situated practices, rendering moral responsibility a persistent human responsibility rather than an autonomous machine capability.
actions.lede: Artificial moral agency is better understood through human delegation and governance structures rather than machine autonomy.
actions.reason: Completing the inquiry into moral agency requirements by synthesizing historical delegation frameworks with contemporary semiotic inquiry.
actions.title: Theoretical Foundations of Artificial Agency and Moral Responsibility
